tour.overview:
Fifty kilometres north-east of Mexico City, Teotihuacan was one of the largest cities in the world around 450 AD, with perhaps 100,000 inhabitants. Who built it is still a mystery; centuries after its fall, the Aztecs found its ruins and named it 'the place where the gods were created'. Its Avenue of the Dead, lined with temples, leads to the Pyramid of the Moon, with the vast Pyramid of the Sun beside it. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

This private day takes you there with a licensed guide and a vehicle, with a stop at the Basilica of Guadalupe, the most visited Catholic shrine in the Americas.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 8 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Mexico City
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; walking in the sun

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Basilica of Guadalupe.
• The Avenue of the Dead.
• The Pyramids of the Sun and the Moon.
• The Temple of the Feathered Serpent.
• The Palace of the Quetzal Butterfly.

WHY THIS WORKS
An early private start brings you to Teotihuacan before the heat and the crowds.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, families and photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a sunrise balloon flight over the pyramids, ask us to add it.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Climbing the Pyramid of the Sun is currently not allowed; the Pyramid of the Moon can be partly climbed when open. There is little shade.

days.name: The Basilica of Guadalupe and the pyramids of Teotihuacan
days.description:
What to expect: the great pre-Hispanic city and Mexico’s great shrine, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrance, a workshop and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:00. On the way north you stop at the Basilica of Our Lady of Guadalupe, where the cloak of Juan Diego, bearing the image of the Virgin said to have appeared to him in 1531, hangs above the altar of the modern basilica, beside the tilting old basilica.

At Teotihuacan, you begin at the Ciudadela and the Temple of the Feathered Serpent, decorated with stone heads of Quetzalcoatl. You walk along the Avenue of the Dead, about 2 kilometres long, to the Pyramid of the Sun, some 65 metres high, and on to the Plaza of the Moon, where the Pyramid of the Moon closes the avenue. Next to it, the Palace of the Quetzal Butterfly has carved pillars and traces of red murals.

At a local workshop, you see how obsidian was worked and how the agave plant gives fibre, paper and drinks, with a tasting of pulque or mezcal. Lunch is at a nearby restaurant, perhaps in a cave, before driving back to Mexico City.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:30 – Basilica of Guadalupe.
10:00 – Teotihuacan: the Feathered Serpent temple.
10:45 – Avenue of the Dead and the Pyramid of the Sun.
12:00 – Plaza and Pyramid of the Moon.
13:00 – Obsidian and agave workshop.
13:45 – Lunch.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A sunrise hot-air balloon flight can be booked; the day then starts at 5:00.
• Bring a hat and sun cream.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrance, workshop and tasting, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: balloon flight, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we climb the pyramids?
faq.answer: Climbing the Pyramid of the Sun is currently not permitted; rules change, and your guide will tell you what is open.

faq.question: Can we add a balloon flight?
Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the pyramids. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The site is large and uneven.

faq.question: How long is the drive?
faq.answer: About 1 hour each way, depending on traffic.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: Only the workshop, with no obligation to buy.

faq.question: Is the Basilica visit respectful?
faq.answer: Yes; services take place throughout the day, and your guide explains the etiquette.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, a hat, sun cream and layers.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: October to May. Early mornings are best all year.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Mexico: 10 to 15 percent for guides and drivers is usual if you were happy with the service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
